extracted.intended_audience: researchers, educators, and policy-makers working on assessment, AI/digital literacy, and open & distance learning in Africa
extracted.subtask_short: ai & digital competency measurement for african odl
extracted.subtask_description: Designing or evaluating frameworks and measurement instruments for AI and digital competencies specifically for large-scale, resource-constrained African open and distance learning (ODL) contexts; includes mapping existing approaches via a PRISMA-ScR scoping review and recommending contextual adaptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive taxonomy and measurement approach (e.g., UNESCO, AICOS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Global frameworks such as UNESCO's AI Competency Framework for Students (2024) and instruments such as the AI Competency Objective Scale (AICOS; Markus et al., 2025) offer comprehensive taxonomies and measurement approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These frameworks provide detailed taxonomies and measurement approaches that can be used as reference models or starting points for competency specification and instrument design. However, the page notes they are often operationally demanding for low-resource contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational feasibility / deployability at scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing global frameworks are operationally demanding and assume infrastructure, data systems, and assessment instruments that most African Open and Distance Learning (ODL) institutions cannot deploy at scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key criterion for any framework or instrument is whether it can be implemented with limited infrastructure and at large scale across ODL systems; designers should prioritise low-infrastructure, low-data approaches and consider logistical constraints when adapting frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualisation for resource-constrained African ODL environments
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need to map current competency assessment approaches and examine how they can be adapted for large-scale, resource-constrained African ODL environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks and measures must be adapted (not simply adopted) to local contexts — including language, technology availability, pedagogical models used in ODL, and institutional capacity. Adaptation guidance should consider cultural relevance, practicality, and alignment with ODL delivery modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on measurable competency (the 'competency divide') rather than access alone
rubrics_metrics.description: As device access and connectivity expand across Africa, distance education institutions face a growing 'competency divide' — a gap not in access, but in measurable digital and AI capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement efforts should prioritise assessing actual competencies and capabilities (skills, understanding, practices) rather than treating access/connectivity as sufficient evidence of competency. Instruments should capture demonstrable ability to use AI/digital tools appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping existing assessment approaches via PRISMA-ScR scoping review
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a PRISMA-ScR scoping review is proposed to map current competency assessment approaches relevant to AI and digital competencies in African ODL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological rigor and transparency in the scoping review (following PRISMA-ScR) is a criterion: clearly defined search and selection procedures, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and synthesis of findings to inform framework development and adaptation recommendations.
